output.brief: The crash gap is mostly a build effect, not a flag effect. Everyone who can have the flag is on build 7.4.0, and 7.4.0 crashes at about 2% versus about 0.7% on 7.3.2. That was already true on 2–3 Sep, before the flag ramp. The top 7.4.0 crash is in the upgraded image library (Pixelda HEIF decoding), and none of the crash clusters involve canvas code. Within 7.4.0, flag-on and holdout users crash at nearly the same rate (2.10% vs 1.98%, difference not significant). Device mix and usage are the same across groups. The app store's own crash counts agree with the crash-reporting tool, so this isn't a counting artifact. The 9 Sep backend deploy didn't change 7.3.2's rate. A small flag effect, a few tenths of a point, can't be ruled out yet. Don't do the plan as written: switching the flag off won't fix anything, and 100% rollout would spread the real crash. Hold 7.4.0 at 25%, fix the Pixelda crash in a new build, and keep the existing holdout running (or widen it) to settle the flag question. Don't roll back the crash-reporting SDK. Confidence is fairly high on the build cause, moderate on the flag's small residual effect.
